brands.name: Ninth Line

brands.name: Madder & Indigo
brands.device: A stitched sampler raster (alphabet, border, wordmark) opens; the kit plan is a band list with roman numerals in the three dye colours on dashed stitch rules.

brands.name: Northline
brands.device: Route diagram raster, then the issue as a line: 20 px yellow spine column with stop rasters and km markers on the left.

brands.name: Low Ohm Records
brands.device: A meter-bridge raster (one VU meter per record, red only past zero) with the three record names set in a stacked three-column row beneath; tour dates as ruled data rows.

brands.name: Fieldbook Seeds
brands.device: Packet masthead on tomato, a seed-packet raster, and a sowing table of zebra data rows (Crop / Sow / Days) under a leaf header row.

brands.name: Devil's Garage
brands.device: Comic-panel stack: every panel sits in a 14/572/14 column row and between 14 px black spacers, so a black outline frames each candy-lacquer panel.

brands.name: Forge & Temper
brands.device: Strike photo then a 6 px heat bar; the stencil headline reads like a stamped batch mark; specs are a dashed-rule spec sheet (label / value).

brands.name: Summit Supply
brands.device: Trail blaze (8 px white / red / white spacers) top and bottom; discounts set as a yellow signpost: altitude bands with percentages, ruled in granite ink.

brands.name: Alpenbahn
brands.device: Red ticket header, departure / duration / arrival row, ticket fields (label over value) in non-stacking rows, a dashed tear line and a tinted stub with the booking reference.

brands.name: Margin Books
brands.device: A 380 px receipt slip on counter grey: Courier lines, 70/30 item and price rows, dashed tear rules, TOTAL at 18 px, the button in the receipt footer.

brands.name: Paper Plane
brands.device: A 560 px kraft page carrying a white label panel (32/496/32 columns): service slab, from/to, black sort-code slab, tracking number, barcode raster.

brands.name: Signal/Noise
brands.device: Black day bars and a 22/78 time / session grid on light rules; one accent (blue) marks keynotes and the headline slab.

brands.name: Harrow & Vale

narrative.overview:
The gallery is a collection, not an identity. Each of the fifteen templates is the email one invented brand would really send, and each is built from an artefact of that brand's own world: a ledger pad, an eye chart, a sampler, a transit diagram, a VU meter bridge, a seed packet, a lowbrow gallery panel, a forge floor, a trail blaze, a rail ticket, a thermal receipt, a shipping label, a conference programme, a provenance ribbon, a CRT high-score screen. No palette, typeface or layout formula is shared across brands; what is shared is the set of construction rules below, which every template obeys and which let any of them survive the worst inbox.

The system therefore lives at two levels. The **house rules** (Layout, Shapes, Components, Do's and Don'ts) are invariant: body-only block JSON, table rendering, square corners, a 40 px content inset, display type in heading blocks only, owned rasters, and a system-font fallback that still reads in-world. The **brand register** (Colors, Typography, and the per-brand tokens in the frontmatter) records each own-world: its artefact colours at page scale, its type pairing with fallback stack, its signature device and its assets.

Density is the artefact's own: a receipt is tight and monospaced, an eye chart is airy and centred, a programme is a grid. The action is found inside the artefact (the ledger's total line, the eye chart's last line, the ticket's stub, the receipt's footer), never in a generic slab bolted on below. The category default the old gallery shipped (photo hero with centred headline and pill button, a row of icon cards, a dark CTA slab, an italic quote) is the confirmed anti-reference.
keyCharacteristics: One brand per template, one artefact per brand, committed at page scale.
Body-only block JSON rendered as tables with inline CSS; 600 px wide (560 and 380 where the artefact is narrower).
Square corners everywhere; no shadows; depth comes from outer ground versus page and from ruled bands.
Display type lives in heading blocks with a named email fallback stack; text blocks carry only body copy.
Photos, art and any lettering are owned, provenance-tagged rasters with alt text.
Realistic sample content: names, prices, codes and dates, never merge tags.

rules.name: The Artefact Palette Rule
rules.body: A brand's colours are the colours of its artefact (ledger green, packet tomato and leaf, rail red, phosphor black), applied at page scale. No colour is borrowed from another brand in the set, and no brand gets a neutral SaaS palette.

rules.name: The Readable Ink Rule
rules.body: Body text and secondary ink hold at least 4.5:1 against the surface they sit on (the softest shipped pairing, Acuity Grey #767676 on white, is 4.54:1). Display lettering of 22 px bold and up may sit on a saturated artefact field at the large-text threshold.

rules.name: The Heading-Block Type Rule
rules.body: Distinctive type is set only on heading blocks (`style.fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textTransform`), because the rich-text editor strips inline styles. Text blocks carry body copy in the template's default font with only per-block `fontSize` and `color`.

rules.name: The Fallback Is the Design Rule
rules.body: Web fonts load only in Apple Mail, iOS Mail and some Android clients. Every family is written with a fallback stack chosen to keep the world (stencil to Arial Narrow, pixel faces to Monaco/Consolas, slab to Rockwell, Garamond to Garamond/Georgia), and the `.nofonts` render must still read as the brand.

rules.name: The Data Rows Don't Stack Rule
rules.body: Any row whose columns are read across (time / session, item / price, rank / initials / score, label / value) sets `stackOnMobile: false`.

rules.name: The Outer-Padding Inset Rule
rules.body: A stacking row takes its inset from outer-column padding, never from a block-level wrapper, so the engine can mirror it symmetrically when stacked.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: Separation is made with ground colour, full-width bands and rules from the artefact (ledger double rules, receipt tear lines, stitch dashes), never with shadow or blur.

dos: **Do** build each template from one artefact of the brand's world and commit its colours at page scale.
**Do** keep templates body-only: header and footer regions empty, masthead and postal footer as body blocks.
**Do** set distinctive type on heading blocks, always with its email fallback stack; leave text blocks to the default font with only `fontSize` and `color`.
**Do** inset content 40 px (32 px at 560 width, 24 px on the 380 px receipt), and give stacking rows that inset as outer-column padding.
**Do** set `stackOnMobile: false` on every data row.

**Do** use owned rasters under `frontend/public/gallery-assets/<brand>/` with provenance embedded and meaningful alt text; letters and numerals inside art are authored rasters (the sampler alphabet, the route-map labels, the barcode), never AI-rendered text.
**Do** write realistic sample values: names, addresses, prices, codes, tracking numbers, dates.
**Do** keep body text and secondary ink at 4.5:1 or better against their surface.
**Do** check every template in its `.nofonts` render; the system-font view must still read in-world.
donts: **Don't** use social or icon blocks: their SVG data URIs do not display in Gmail or Outlook. Use text links.
**Don't** use merge tags (`{{first_name}}`) in gallery templates.
**Don't** put inline styles or font families inside text-block rich text; the editor strips them.
**Don't** round corners or add shadows; Outlook desktop drops both and no artefact here needs them.
**Don't** put an eyebrow label above a heading. Field captions that belong to the artefact (ticket and label fields, table column heads) sit with their value, not as kickers over a headline.
**Don't** open with a full-bleed photo hero with centred copy, a row of icon cards, a dark CTA slab or an italic quote.
**Don't** share a palette, type voice or layout formula between two templates.
**Don't** hotlink or use expiring image URLs.
